sections.h2: Selling a Neenah house on your own schedule
sections.html:
Neenah sellers choose between an agent, going solo and a cash buyer who wants the house exactly as it stands. Time on your hands and a move-in-ready home point to a listing. A tired house, an estate or a closing date set in stone points to a direct sale.

The city is home to 27,638 people, and owners live in about 66.2 percent of its homes. The 2020 to 2024 median owner-occupied value was $210,700, owners with a mortgage paid a median of $1,415 a month, and median household income was $75,374. At 9.37 square miles, Neenah is compact, and the average commute is 18.1 minutes. Buyers who work nearby may value that.

sections.h2: The assessor and your home's record
sections.html:
Assessment questions go to the Division of Community Development, 211 Walnut St., Room 313. Appointments are booked at 920-886-6115 or assessors@neenahwi.gov. Staff there look after non-waterfront homes. Waterfront residential and commercial properties belong to a statutory assessor from Associated Appraisal Consultants, Inc., at 920-749-1995.

An appraiser who visits to verify records carries city photo identification and drives a city vehicle. Did a letter from the office arrive while you were getting ready to sell? Book the visit. Correct counts of bedrooms, finished space and additions mean fewer surprises when the buyer's side does its homework. The office's page also links the Department of Revenue guide for property owners.

Neenah's planning forms page lists a Tourist House Permit for short-term rentals, along with a home occupation application and a driveway standards sheet. If guests have stayed at your house, ask Community Development about the permit status before you advertise the property as a rental, and ask whether a permit can move to a new owner.

The same page links the zoning application used for site plan review, rezoning and plats. Building permits are handled by the Inspections division, so call it if a past owner finished work without one.

Pull these together early so a buyer or title company is not waiting on you.

  • The parcel identification number from your tax bill, which belongs on the deed.
  • The current-year tax bill and any special assessment figures.
  • Permit records for work done on the house. Call the Inspections division if a past owner finished work with no permit.
  • Any Tourist House Permit paperwork if guests ever stayed.
  • A corrected assessment record if the Assessment office sent you a letter about your house.

The Neenah Joint School District has one high school, one middle school and several elementary options, including Alliance Charter School and Clayton, Coolidge, Horace Mann, Lakeview, Spring Road, Taft and Tullar elementary schools, plus the Washington School of Early Learning. Look at the boundary map for grades K to 4 to see which elementary school covers a particular address, and mention it when you list.

If you are selling a property with one to four units, Wis. Stat. 709.02 wants a real estate condition report in the buyer's hands inside 10 days of acceptance. A buyer who never receives it can rescind during the two business days after that. A report is complete only once you have answered, or supplied information for, every single item.

The transfer fee under Wis. Stat. 77.22 is 30 cents per $100. You owe it as the grantor, and the register collects it along with the deed. Some transfers escape it.

  • Deeds in lieu of foreclosure and transfers by will or survivorship carry no fee.
  • Section 77.25 also exempts family transfers for nominal or no consideration, like parent to child. A plain sale to a relative is taxed anyway.
  • If the fee is not owed, write the reason on the face of the deed.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Winnebago County
sections.html:
Winnebago County records Neenah deeds, and its Register of Deeds is strict about form.

What a Winnebago County deed needs
RequirementDetail
PartiesGrantor and grantee named
SignatureNotarized grantor signature
PropertyLegal description, plus the parcel identification number from the tax bill under the return address
Return addressShown on the deed
OriginalOriginal deed with original signatures only. Photocopies are refused.
Recording fee$30

Bring the Wisconsin transfer return receipt with the deed, plus the recording fee and any transfer fee. The office number is 920-232-3394. Staff give general guidance only. They will not answer legal questions or show you how to fill out the return, so let an attorney or title company draft the deed.

sections.h2: Property tax dates and the closing split
sections.html:
Wisconsin sets value as of January 1 and mails bills by the third Monday in December. Pay the first installment by January 31 and the second by July 31. Unpaid tax collects interest of 1 percent a month, counted from February 1.

Get the current bill and any special assessments from the City of Neenah or the Winnebago County treasurer. The closing agent will then divide the tax between you and the buyer.

Taking cash costs some price and buys speed and certainty. There are no open houses, no waiting on a buyer's loan and no repair haggling, so closing hinges on title work. A listing puts the house before the most buyers, and Neenah's lake and river settings attract people who finance.

  • Have the offer written down, including the closing date and who pays title costs.
  • Take your mortgage payoff, unpaid taxes and any liens off the price to find your net.
  • Set that net against what a listing would leave once repairs and time on the market are counted.

The condition report is your first deadline after accepting an offer. Answer every item, since a half-finished report does not count as complete. At the same time, request the current tax bill and any special assessment figures, and agree with the buyer on who pays for title work.

Next, an attorney or title company prepares the deed from the parcel number on your tax bill. You file the transfer return and take the receipt to the Register of Deeds with the $30 recording fee and any transfer fee. Only the original deed, with original signatures, can be recorded.

If you are selling for cash, none of this disappears. What changes is the front of the process: there is no mortgage underwriting to wait for, and the buyer does not ask for a repair list.

faqs.a: Winnebago County. Its Register of Deeds charges a flat $30 recording fee and requires an electronic transfer return receipt with each deed.

faqs.q: Who handles assessments for Neenah waterfront homes?
faqs.a: A statutory assessor from Associated Appraisal Consultants, Inc. covers residential waterfront and commercial property. City assessment staff at 920-886-6115 handle non-waterfront residential property.

faqs.q: Does Neenah have a permit for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's planning forms page lists a Tourist House Permit. Ask Community Development whether your property has one before you sell.
The Neenah Joint School District, with Neenah High School, Neenah Middle School and several elementary schools. A K to 4 boundary map shows which elementary school covers an address.

faqs.q: How much is the Wisconsin transfer fee on a Neenah sale?
faqs.a: It is 30 cents per $100 of value, paid by the seller, unless an exemption applies.
